import os
import math
import numpy as np
import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.robot as turtlebot
from pychrono import irrlicht as chronoirr

# Create Chrono system
system = chrono.ChSystemNSC()
system.SetCollisionSystemType(chrono.ChCollisionSystem.Type_BULLET)
system.SetGravitationalAcceleration(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, -9.81))  # Set gravity in negative Z direction
chrono.ChCollisionModel.SetDefaultSuggestedEnvelope(0.0025)
chrono.ChCollisionModel.SetDefaultSuggestedMargin(0.0025)

# Create ground body as terrain plane that robot will drive on
ground_mat = chrono.ChContactMaterialNSC()
ground = chrono.ChBodyEasyBox(20, 20, 1, 1000, True, True, ground_mat)
ground.SetPos(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, -1))  # Position the ground slightly below the origin
ground.SetFixed(True)  # Fix the ground in place
ground.GetVisualShape(0).SetTexture(chrono.GetChronoDataFile("textures/concrete.jpg"))
system.Add(ground)

# Create Turtlebot Robot
init_pos = chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0.2, 0)  # Initial position of the robot
init_rot = chrono.ChQuaterniond(1, 0, 0, 0)  # Initial orientation of the robot
robot = turtlebot.TurtleBot(system, init_pos, init_rot)  # Create Turtlebot instance
robot.Initialize()  # Initialize the robot

# Create run-time visualization
vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(system)
vis.SetCameraVertical(chrono.CameraVerticalDir_Z)
vis.SetWindowSize(1280, 720)
vis.SetWindowTitle('Turtlebot Robot - Rigid terrain')
vis.Initialize()
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile('logo_pychrono_alpha.png'))
vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 1.5, 0.2), chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0.2))
vis.AddTypicalLights()
vis.AddLightWithShadow(chrono.ChVector3d(1.5, -2.5, 5.5), chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0.5), 3, 4, 10, 40, 512)

# Enable shadows (commented out to improve performance)
# vis.EnableShadows()

# Set the simulation time step
time_step = 2e-3

# Simulation loop
time = 0
while vis.Run():
    # Define WheelID enum values for motor control
    LEFT_DRIVE_WHEEL = 0
    RIGHT_DRIVE_WHEEL = 1
    
    # At time = 1 s, start left turn
    if abs(time - 1.0) < 1e-4:
        robot.SetMotorSpeed(0, LEFT_DRIVE_WHEEL)
        robot.SetMotorSpeed(-math.pi, RIGHT_DRIVE_WHEEL)
        
    # At time = 2 s, start right turn
    if abs(time - 2.0) < 1e-4:
        robot.SetMotorSpeed(-math.pi, LEFT_DRIVE_WHEEL)
        robot.SetMotorSpeed(0, RIGHT_DRIVE_WHEEL)

    # Increment time counter
    time += time_step

    # Render the scene
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()

    # Advance the simulation by one time step
    system.DoStepDynamics(time_step)

```python
import os
import math
import numpy as np
import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.robot as turtlebot
from pychrono import irrlicht as chronoirr
import pychrono.sensor as sens

# Create Chrono system
system = chrono.ChSystemNSC()
system.SetCollisionSystemType(chrono.ChCollisionSystem.Type_BULLET)
system.SetGravitationalAcceleration(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, -9.81))  # Set gravity in negative Z direction
chrono.ChCollisionModel.SetDefaultSuggestedEnvelope(0.0025)
chrono.ChCollisionModel.SetDefaultSuggestedMargin(0.0025)

# Create ground body as terrain plane that robot will drive on
ground_mat = chrono.ChContactMaterialNSC()
ground = chrono.ChBodyEasyBox(20, 20, 1, 1000, True, True, ground_mat)
ground.SetPos(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, -0.6))  # Position the ground slightly below the origin
ground.SetFixed(True)  # Fix the ground in place
ground.GetVisualShape(0).SetTexture(chrono.GetChronoDataFile("textures/concrete.jpg"))
system.Add(ground)

# Create Turtlebot Robot
init_pos = chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0.2, 0)  # Initial position of the robot
init_rot = chrono.ChQuaternionD(1, 0, 0, 0)  # Initial orientation of the robot
robot = turtlebot.TurtleBot(system, init_pos, init_rot)  # Create Turtlebot instance
robot.Initialize()  # Initialize the robot

# Create run-time visualization
vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(system)
vis.SetCameraVertical(chrono.CameraVerticalDir_Z)
vis.SetWindowSize(1280, 720)
vis.SetWindowTitle('Turtlebot Robot - Rigid terrain')
vis.Initialize()
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile('logo_pychrono_alpha.png'))
vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 1.5, 0.2), chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0.2))
vis.AddTypicalLights()
vis.AddLightWithShadow(chrono.ChVectorD(1.5, -2.5, 5.5), chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0.5), 3, 4, 10, 40, 512)

# Enable shadows
vis.EnableShadows()

# Set the simulation time step
time_step = 2e-3

# Create sensor manager
sensor_manager = sens.ChSensorManager(system)

# Add lidar sensor
lidar = sens.ChLidarSensor(system, 100, 0.01, 0.5, 100, sens.ChLidarSensor.Type.TYPE_LIDAR)
lidar.SetPos(chrono.ChVectorD(0.2, 0.2, 0.5))
sensor_manager.AddSensor(lidar)
system.Add(sensor_manager)

# Add randomly placed boxes
boxes = []
for i in range(5):
    box = chrono.ChBodyEasyBox(0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 1000, True, True)
    box.SetPos(chrono.ChVectorD(np.random.uniform(-5, 5), np.random.uniform(-5, 5), 0))
    box.SetColor(chrono.ChColor(np.random.uniform(0, 1), np.random.uniform(0, 1), np.random.uniform(0, 1)))
    box.SetBodyFixed(True)
    system.Add(box)
    boxes.append(box)

# Define motion control function
def move(mode):
    if mode == 'straight':
        robot.SetMotorSpeed(1, 0)
        robot.SetMotorSpeed(1, 1)
    elif mode == 'left':
        robot.SetMotorSpeed(-math.pi/2, 0)
        robot.SetMotorSpeed(-math.pi/2, 1)
    elif mode == 'right':
        robot.SetMotorSpeed(math.pi/2, 0)
        robot.SetMotorSpeed(math.pi/2, 1)

# Simulation loop
time = 0
while vis.Run():
    if time > 1.0:
        move('left')
    elif time > 2.0:
        move('right')
    elif time > 3.0:
        move('straight')
        
    time += time_step

    # Update sensor manager
    sensor_manager.Update()

    # Render the scene
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()

    # Advance the simulation by one time step
    system.DoStepDynamics(time_step)
```

The simulation loop has been updated to use the motion control function and to update the sensor manager.

Let's start by importing the necessary modules:

```python
from pychrono importchrono as ch
from pychrono.core import ChSystem, ChFrameD, ChVectorD, ChQuaternionD
from pychrono.irrlicht import ChIrrApp
from pychrono.geometry import ChTriangleMeshShape, ChTriangleMeshAsset
from pychrono.engine import ChMotor
from pychrono.rigidbody import ChBodyEasy

# Initialize the PyChrono system
chrono_system = ChSystem()
```

### Step 2: Set up the Chrono system with gravity and a ground body

```python
# Gravity
chrono_system.Set_G_acc(ChVectorD(0, -9.81, 0))

# Create a ground plane
ground_shape = ChTriangleMeshShape()
ground_shape.SetMesh(ChTriangleMeshAsset(chrono_system, "data/ground.obj"))
ground_body = ChBodyEasyMesh(ground_shape, 1000, 0, 0, True)
ground_body.SetPos(ChVectorD(0, 0, 0))
ground_body.SetBodyFixed(True)
chrono_system.Add(ground_body)
```

### Step 3: Create the Turtlebot robot and place it on the ground

```python
# Define Turtlebot parameters
turtlebot_mass = 10.0
turtlebot_length = 0.5
turtlebot_width = 0.5
turtlebot_height = 0.2
turtlebot_pos = ChVectorD(0, 0, turtlebot_height / 2)
turtlebot_rot = ChQuaternionD(1, 0, 0, 0)

# Create Turtlebot
turtlebot = ChBodyEasyCylinder(turtlebot_mass, turtlebot_length / 2, turtlebot_height, True, True)
turtlebot.SetPos(turtlebot_pos)
turtlebot.SetRot(ChQuaternionD(1, 0, 0, 0))
turtlebot.SetBodyFixed(False)
chrono_system.Add(turtlebot)

# Add motors to control left and right wheels
left_motor = ChMotor()
right_motor = ChMotor()
left_motor.SetMass(turtlebot_mass)
right_motor.SetMass(turtlebot_mass)
left_motor.SetGearRatio(1)
right_motor.SetGearRatio(1)
left_motor.SetTorque(0)
right_motor.SetTorque(0)

# Attach motors to the wheels
# Assuming the wheels are at the ends of the Turtlebot
left_wheel = ChBodyEasyCylinder(0.05, 0.05, turtlebot_height, True, True)
left_wheel.SetPos(ChVectorD(-turtlebot_length / 2, 0, turtlebot_height / 2))
left_wheel.SetRot(ChQuaternionD(1, 0, 0, 0))
left_wheel.SetBodyFixed(False)
chrono_system.Add(left_wheel)
left_wheel.SetMotor(left_motor)

right_wheel = ChBodyEasyCylinder(0.05, 0.05, turtlebot_height, True, True)
right_wheel.SetPos(ChVectorD(turtlebot_length / 2, 0, turtlebot_height / 2))
right_wheel.SetRot(ChQuaternionD(1, 0, 0, 0))
right_wheel.SetBodyFixed(False)
chrono_system.Add(right_wheel)
right_wheel.SetMotor(right_motor)
```

### Step 4: Initialize the Irrlicht visualization engine

```python
# Visualization
app = ChIrrApp(chrono_system, "PyChrono Turtlebot Simulation", ChVectorD(800, 600), False)
app.AddTypicalSky()
app.AddTypicalLogo("logo.ppm")
app.AddTypicalCamera(ChVectorD(0, 10, 10))
app.AddTypicalLights()
app.AssetBindAll()
app.AssetUpdateAll()
```

### Step 5: Simulation loop with motor control

```python
# Simulation loop parameters
simulation_duration = 10  # seconds
timestep = 1e-3  # 1 ms

# Simulation loop
for step in range(int(simulation_duration / timestep)):
    # Simulate the system
    chrono_system.DoStepDynamics(timestep)
    
    # Motor control (example: turn left for 1 second, then turn right for 1 second)
    if step < 2:
        left_motor.SetTorque(-1)  # Left turn
        right_motor.SetTorque(1)  # Right turn
    else:
        left_motor.SetTorque(1)  # Right turn
        right_motor.SetTorque(-1)  # Left turn
    
    # Update and render the scene
    app.BeginScene()
    app.DrawAll()
    app.EndScene()
```

This script sets up a basic PyChrono simulation with a Turtlebot robot on a ground plane, controlled by motors for left and right turns, and visualized in real-time using Irrlicht.
